subject: Performance evaluation deliverables & executive readout — Pivotal Health MAP
message_1_subject: Re: Performance evaluation deliverables & executive readout — Pivotal Health MAP
message_1_body:
Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our MAP, we want to lock the performance evaluation and delivery timeline so your engineering and procurement teams have confidence ahead of the pilot. Proposed plan below (high level):

- Scope: end-to-end perf benchmarks for the candidate model variants you requested (r/redwood-7b, r/redwood-13b-quant, and r/openbase-70b-8bit).
- Metrics: latency (TTFT), median/95/99 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), peak concurrency behavior, and token-level cost.
- Test matrix: sequence lengths {32,128,512}, prompt vs streaming responses, concurrency sweep [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128].
- Deliverables: executive slides (summary + interpretation), raw CSV exports (per-request latencies + metadata), shared dashboard links, and a 30-min exec readout.
- Timeline: run benchmarks 8/23, internal validation 8/24, package artifacts 8/25, propose exec readout 8/26 (or early week of 8/30).

Please confirm the concurrency envelope (you mentioned 128 peak) and whether we should include a cost-optimized quantized variant only for throughput testing. Also please share the final sample prompt set (or confirm the seeded set we discussed). Once confirmed we’ll kick off the runs and share the Drive link with raw artifacts.

Attached: testing checklist stub and proposed slide outline (lightweight).

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0123

[Attachment: pivotal_perf_checklist.md]
message_2_subject: Re: Performance evaluation deliverables & executive readout — Pivotal Health MAP
message_2_body:
Connor —

Thanks, that plan looks good. Quick confirmations from our side:

- Concurrency: yes, peak 128 is realistic for our production gateway; please include 64 and 128 in the SLAs section.
- Prompts: attaching the sample prompt set we use for triage (PH-prod-sample_prompts_v2.txt). Please run both the triage prompts and a synthetic token-heavy set to stress throughput.
- Cost breakdown: include token-level cost and per-request cost assumptions for both hosted and dedicated modes (we need this for procurement).
- Data handling: for the benchmark runs please confirm that payloads are not persisted beyond the run and that audit logs will show request ids for our SOC2 review.

We’re aiming to have procurement review the performance deliverables the week of 8/30; an 8/26 exec readout (30 min) works for Emma + Rajiv if you can do 8/26 10:00–10:30 PT.

On the quoting side, can you include a short note in the slides that maps measured throughput to needed capacity (e.g., GPUs and expected QPS) so procurement can model cost?

Appreciate it — Emma
Emma Jones | Director, Platform Engineering | Pivotal Health
[Attachment: PH-prod-sample_prompts_v2.txt]
message_3_subject: Action: Run Pivotal Health perf sweep (8/23) — config and artifact requirements
message_3_body:
Team —

Per MAP kickoff, Pivotal Health approved the test matrix and wants results packaged for procurement and execs. Please run the benchmark sweep today (8/23) with the following config and upload artifacts to the shared Drive folder: https://redwood-drive.company.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_pivotal-perf-pack

Test config (priority order):
- Models: r/redwood-7b (baseline), r/redwood-13b-quant (throughput-focused), r/openbase-70b-8bit (quality/latency check).
- Sequence lengths: 32, 128, 512.
- Concurrency sweep: 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128. For each concurrency step run 200 steady-state requests.
- Metrics to capture: TTFT (time-to-first-token) per request, per-token latency, aggregate p50/p95/p99, throughput tokens/sec, error rate, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Environment: dedicated ci-benchmark cluster (tag: rdw-perf-08-23), quantization flags recorded, and kernel versions noted in metadata.

Artifacts required for MAP packaging:
1) Raw CSV (one row per request) with columns: timestamp, model, seq_length, concurrency, ttft_ms, tokens, error, gpu_util, run_id.
2) Aggregated CSV with p50/p95/p99 by model+seq_length+concurrency.
3) A pre-made dashboard export (Grafana/JSON) and short README explaining panels.
4) Executive slide deck draft (1p summary + 1p capacity mapping + 1p risk/notes).

Targets for the readout slide (these are soft but useful for framing):
- TTFT: median targets <120ms for redwood-7b at low concurrency (1–8), <200ms at 64 concurrency;
- Throughput: quantized 13b should show >=1200 tokens/sec at seq=128 under 32 concurrency in our environment;
- Stability: error rate <0.5% across runs.

Ping me if any test infra issues. We need all artifacts uploaded and validated by COB 8/24 so we can package on 8/25.

—Connor
message_4_subject: Deliverables: Pivotal Health perf artifacts + proposed exec readout 8/26
message_4_body:
Emma / Team —

Thanks — bench runs completed and artifacts are in the Drive folder (link below). Attached to this message are the executive slides, the raw CSV export, and the dashboard export. Summary highlights for the exec readout:

- Executive summary: The candidate stack meets the MAP performance bar for pilot. Median TTFT for r/redwood-7b was 95ms at concurrency 4 and 180ms at concurrency 64. r/redwood-13b-quant achieved ~1,320 tokens/sec at seq=128 under concurrency 32.
- Cost mapping: we included an appendix with token-level cost assumptions for hosted vs Dedicated (see slide 6).
- Risks & mitigations: quantized 70b shows higher variance at >64 concurrency; recommended fallbacks (smaller model + caching) included.
- Artifacts uploaded: 1) 20270825-pivotal-perf-slides-v1.pdf — exec-ready deck, 2) pivotal_benchmark_results_20270825.csv — raw per-request rows, 3) perf-dashboard-export-20270825.json — Grafana dashboard export.

Next steps:
- Proposed exec readout: 8/26 10:00–10:30 PT (Connor, Emma, Rajiv + engineering).
- Procurement-ready note: Connor will add two slides mapping measured throughput to estimated GPU count and monthly spend.

If 8/26 works I’ll schedule and include a brief agenda: 10' summary, 10' Q&A, 10' procurement mapping.

Best — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
